title: Insulation Rebates in Cape Breton 2026: Up to $1,500 for Walls
desc: Cape Breton insulation rebates for 2026: attic up to $750, walls up to $1,500, basement up to $1,200, air sealing $200, or free through HomeWarming. For CBRM's older homes.
lead: Two out of three Cape Breton households live in homes built before 1981, and one in five in homes built before 1946. In houses that age, insulation and air sealing often save more than any new equipment. Efficiency Nova Scotia pays for both. Here is what a Cape Breton homeowner can claim.
cards_heading: What insulation rebates pay in Cape Breton
cards_intro: From Efficiency Nova Scotia's Home Energy Assessment rebate guide (August 2026), still linked from its program page on October 3, 2026. Amounts are maximums, paid on the share of the area you insulate. We found no extra rebate from Cape Breton Regional Municipality.

cards.title: Attic
cards.note: For bringing the attic up to R-50.

cards.title: Exterior walls
cards.note: Pro-rated by the share of wall area insulated. Full amount for detached houses.

cards.title: Moderate Income Rebate
cards.note: Homes heated mainly by oil, propane or other non-electric fuel, under the income limits. Pre-approval required.

cards.title: HomeWarming
cards.note: Lower-income homeowners get insulation and draft-proofing at no charge.

after_cards:
A detached Glace Bay house, worked out

A detached house insulates its attic to R-50, all its exterior walls and its basement walls, and gets air sealed. The maximums add up to $750 + $1,500 + $1,200 + $200 = $3,650, inside the $5,000 assessment cap and never more than the work cost. Because it is detached, the house gets the full wall and basement amounts. Semis and end units get 75%, and middle row units 50%.
sections:
Statistics Canada's 2021 Census counted 42,310 households in Cape Breton Regional Municipality. About 28,645 of them, 68%, live in homes built before 1981, and 8,705, about 21%, in homes built before 1946. Homes from those years were built before modern energy codes. The census also found 9.3% of households in homes that need major repairs, higher than Halifax's 6.4%.

The housing is also mostly detached: about 74% of households, versus 48% in Halifax. That matters for the rebate, because detached houses get the full amount for walls and foundations. It also matters for the bill, because a detached house loses heat through four walls, a roof and a basement.

Book an initial Home Energy Assessment ($199, waived for moderate-income households) before any work starts. An energy advisor checks your insulation, air leakage and heating system and gives you a report. You do the work within 12 months, then book a final assessment, and the rebate is paid on what was added. The home must be at least six months old.

In an older house, the report often matters as much as the rebate. It shows whether the walls are empty, whether the basement is losing heat, and where air is getting in. Doing the shell before a heat pump can mean a smaller, cheaper heat pump later.

Many Cape Breton households should check the income programs first. HomeWarming arranges and pays for insulation and draft-proofing for lower-income homeowners, with after-tax limits of $30,187 for one person, $57,075 for two to four people and $79,163 for five or more. Waits can be long, so apply early.

The Moderate Income Rebate adds up to $5,000 for homes heated mainly by oil, propane or another non-electric fuel, with limits from $37,260 for one person up to $126,500 for five or more. Wood stoves don't count as the primary heat source. Apply and get approved before the work starts.

Tighter homes can change indoor air, including radon. Efficiency Nova Scotia suggests testing for radon, and an HRV, which brings in fresh air, earns $300 through the assessment.
claim_heading: How to get an insulation rebate in Cape Breton
claim_steps: Check your income against the HomeWarming and Moderate Income Rebate limits, and apply first if you qualify.
Book a Home Energy Assessment before any work starts.
Get quotes for the upgrades in your report. Ask each contractor what R-value and area they will cover.
Book the final assessment to get paid.
faq: How much is the insulation rebate in Cape Breton?
Up to $750 for the attic, $1,500 for exterior walls, $1,200 for basement walls and $960 for a crawlspace, plus $200 for air sealing, through Efficiency Nova Scotia's Home Energy Assessment.
Does Cape Breton Regional Municipality have its own insulation rebate?
We found none. Cape Breton homes use the provincial Efficiency Nova Scotia programs.
Is there free insulation in Cape Breton?
Yes, for lower-income homeowners through HomeWarming. It covers insulation and draft-proofing at no charge.
Can I do the insulation first and apply after?
No. The initial assessment must happen before work starts, and the final assessment after.
